Hi neighbors, this is Cascade Legal Rights Project. Thank you to the moderator for inviting us to respond, and thank you to everyone who raised this. If you asked for help with an eviction and then got a letter from a law firm you'd never heard of, of course that's alarming. You're right to ask questions, and we want to answer them plainly.

**We do not share, sell, or give out information about people who come to our clinics.** Our policy specifically prohibits disclosing attendee information to landlords or their attorneys. Sign-in records stay inside our organization and are kept in locked storage.

**Where these letters most likely come from.** When an eviction (dispossessory) case is filed in magistrate court, the filing becomes a public record. That record includes the tenant's name and address. Some law firms watch new filings and send mailings to the tenants named in them. That's the most likely reason people are getting these letters soon after a case is filed, whether or not they've talked to anyone about it. We know the timing can make it look connected to the clinic.

We won't discuss anyone's individual situation here, even to explain ourselves. Protecting your privacy matters more to us than winning an argument online.

**The clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, 10am to 1pm, but it has moved.** The library meeting room is closed for repairs that day, so we'll be at the **Mt Zion Fellowship hall** in East Atlanta. There's an accessible side entrance by the parking lot. As always it's free and walk-in, and you don't need an appointment. Volunteer attorneys and staff can look over eviction notices and court papers with you and explain your options.

If you're behind on rent or have received court papers, you're welcome on Saturday. If you'd like to talk with us first, about this or about anything else, email clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187.

Cascade Legal Rights Project
